The compiled fallback reproduces the original social-only behavior, which need not be conservative.

Proof.

Immediate from Lemma 3 and Theorem 7. ∎

8.5 Routers, enforcement, and router-level normal form

PBRC is designed to be enforceable: a system-level router (or “output gate”) can reject belief changes that are not justified by a verifiable, nonempty evidence witness. The audit-equivalence notion in Section 8 compares canonicalized certificates, but it does not yet capture the operational effect of enforcement, where the gate may override a proposed update and force fallback. We now formalize this enforcement semantics and show that it induces a canonical evidence-gated normal form.

Witnessed protocols.

Throughout this subsection, we treat a trigger protocol as equipped with fixed witness extractors. Formally, fix an agent ii and a trigger protocol

Pi=⟨(ψi,1,Vi,1),…,(ψi,ri,Vi,ri),≺i,δi⟩P_{i}=\langle(\psi_{i,1},V_{i,1}),\dots,(\psi_{i,r_{i}},V_{i,r_{i}}),\prec_{i},\delta_{i}\rangle

together with witness extractors Witψi,j\mathrm{Wit}_{\psi_{i,j}} satisfying Definition 18. Define the induced certificate map πPi\pi_{P_{i}} by

πPi​(E):={(jPi⋆​(E),Witψi,jPi⋆​(E)​(E)),JPi​(E)≠∅,(⊥,∅),JPi​(E)=∅,\pi_{P_{i}}(E):=\begin{cases}\big(j^{\star}_{P_{i}}(E),\ \mathrm{Wit}_{\psi_{i,j^{\star}_{P_{i}}(E)}}(E)\big),&J_{P_{i}}(E)\neq\emptyset,\\ (\bot,\emptyset),&J_{P_{i}}(E)=\emptyset,\end{cases}

where JPi​(E)J_{P_{i}}(E) and jPi⋆​(E)j^{\star}_{P_{i}}(E) are as in (2). As before, can\mathrm{can} denotes certificate canonicalization (Definition 20).

Definition 23 (Nonempty-witness enforcement (output gate)).

Fix a witnessed trigger protocol PiP_{i} with fallback δi\delta_{i} and certificate map πPi\pi_{P_{i}}. The gate-enforced one-step update is

FPi𝗀𝖺𝗍𝖾​(b,E):={FPi​(b,E),can⁡(πPi​(E))≠(⊥,∅),δi​(b,E),can⁡(πPi​(E))=(⊥,∅).F^{\mathsf{gate}}_{P_{i}}(b,E)\;:=\;\begin{cases}F_{P_{i}}(b,E),&\mathrm{can}(\pi_{P_{i}}(E))\neq(\bot,\emptyset),\\ \delta_{i}(b,E),&\mathrm{can}(\pi_{P_{i}}(E))=(\bot,\emptyset).\end{cases}

This idealized gate is applied to the honestly computed FPiF_{P_{i}} and its specified extractor. It preserves that candidate update iff the certificate is nonempty; otherwise it forces fallback. It is not a validator for arbitrary untrusted certificates or arbitrary agent-supplied numerical outputs.

Definition 24 (Evidence-gated compilation).

Given Pi=⟨(ψi,1,Vi,1),…,(ψi,ri,Vi,ri),≺i,δi⟩P_{i}=\langle(\psi_{i,1},V_{i,1}),\dots,(\psi_{i,r_{i}},V_{i,r_{i}}),\prec_{i},\delta_{i}\rangle, define the evidence-gated PBRC contract

EG(Pi):=⟨(ψi,1∧¬SocialOnly,Vi,1),…,(ψi,ri∧¬SocialOnly,Vi,ri),≺i,δi⟩.\mathrm{EG}(P_{i})\;:=\;\langle(\psi_{i,1}\land\neg\mathrm{SocialOnly},V_{i,1}),\dots,(\psi_{i,r_{i}}\land\neg\mathrm{SocialOnly},V_{i,r_{i}}),\prec_{i},\delta_{i}\rangle.

That is, EG⁡(Pi)\mathrm{EG}(P_{i}) differs from PiP_{i} only by conjoining ¬SocialOnly\neg\mathrm{SocialOnly} to every trigger; the fallback is unchanged.

Theorem 8 (Router normal form (output-gated equivalence)).

Assume the witness extractors Witψi,j\mathrm{Wit}_{\psi_{i,j}} satisfy token soundness and non-vacuity on non-social satisfaction (Definition 18). Then for all beliefs bb and events EE,

FPi𝗀𝖺𝗍𝖾​(b,E)=FEG⁡(Pi)​(b,E).F^{\mathsf{gate}}_{P_{i}}(b,E)\;=\;F_{\mathrm{EG}(P_{i})}(b,E).

Consequently, for any event stream (Et)t≥0(E^{t})_{t\geq 0} and initial belief b0b^{0}, the belief trajectory produced by running PiP_{i} under the nonempty-witness gate is identical to the belief trajectory produced by running the evidence-gated contract EG⁡(Pi)\mathrm{EG}(P_{i}) without an external gate.

Proof.

Fix bb and EE. We proceed by cases.

Case 1: SocialOnly⁡(E)\mathrm{SocialOnly}(E). Then 𝒯⁡(E)=∅\mathcal{T}(E)=\emptyset. By token soundness (Definition 18), every extracted witness set is empty; in particular, if JPi​(E)≠∅J_{P_{i}}(E)\neq\emptyset then πPi​(E)=(j,∅)\pi_{P_{i}}(E)=(j,\emptyset) for some label jj, hence can⁡(πPi​(E))=(⊥,∅)\mathrm{can}(\pi_{P_{i}}(E))=(\bot,\emptyset), while if JPi​(E)=∅J_{P_{i}}(E)=\emptyset then πPi​(E)=(⊥,∅)\pi_{P_{i}}(E)=(\bot,\emptyset) already. In either subcase, Definition 23 yields

FPi𝗀𝖺𝗍𝖾​(b,E)=δi​(b,E).F^{\mathsf{gate}}_{P_{i}}(b,E)=\delta_{i}(b,E).

For EG⁡(Pi)\mathrm{EG}(P_{i}), each compiled trigger contains the conjunct ¬SocialOnly\neg\mathrm{SocialOnly}, which is false in this case, so no trigger is satisfied and the contract outputs fallback:

FEG⁡(Pi)​(b,E)=δi​(b,E).F_{\mathrm{EG}(P_{i})}(b,E)=\delta_{i}(b,E).

Thus the two sides agree.

Case 2: ¬SocialOnly⁡(E)\neg\mathrm{SocialOnly}(E). Then for every jj, E⊧(ψi,j∧¬SocialOnly)E\models(\psi_{i,j}\land\neg\mathrm{SocialOnly}) iff E⊧ψi,jE\models\psi_{i,j}. Hence JEG⁡(Pi)​(E)=JPi​(E)J_{\mathrm{EG}(P_{i})}(E)=J_{P_{i}}(E) and, when nonempty, both select the same highest-priority trigger j⋆j^{\star}.

If JPi​(E)=∅J_{P_{i}}(E)=\emptyset, then both PiP_{i} and EG⁡(Pi)\mathrm{EG}(P_{i}) apply fallback, and

FPi𝗀𝖺𝗍𝖾​(b,E)=δi​(b,E)=FEG⁡(Pi)​(b,E).F^{\mathsf{gate}}_{P_{i}}(b,E)=\delta_{i}(b,E)=F_{\mathrm{EG}(P_{i})}(b,E).

If JPi​(E)≠∅J_{P_{i}}(E)\neq\emptyset, let j⋆=jPi⋆​(E)=jEG⁡(Pi)⋆​(E)j^{\star}=j^{\star}_{P_{i}}(E)=j^{\star}_{\mathrm{EG}(P_{i})}(E). Since E⊧ψi,j⋆E\models\psi_{i,j^{\star}} and ¬SocialOnly⁡(E)\neg\mathrm{SocialOnly}(E), non-vacuity implies Witψi,j⋆​(E)≠∅\mathrm{Wit}_{\psi_{i,j^{\star}}}(E)\neq\emptyset, so can⁡(πPi​(E))≠(⊥,∅)\mathrm{can}(\pi_{P_{i}}(E))\neq(\bot,\emptyset) and the gate accepts:

FPi𝗀𝖺𝗍𝖾​(b,E)=FPi​(b,E)=Vi,j⋆​(b,E).F^{\mathsf{gate}}_{P_{i}}(b,E)=F_{P_{i}}(b,E)=V_{i,j^{\star}}(b,E).

The evidence-gated contract EG⁡(Pi)\mathrm{EG}(P_{i}) also applies Vi,j⋆V_{i,j^{\star}} on this event, so FEG⁡(Pi)​(b,E)=Vi,j⋆​(b,E)F_{\mathrm{EG}(P_{i})}(b,E)=V_{i,j^{\star}}(b,E). Thus the two sides agree.

Since the one-step outputs coincide for all (b,E)(b,E), equality of full trajectories follows by induction over time. ∎

From “nonempty” gates to full routers.

The gate in Definition 23 only inspects whether the witness is nonempty after canonicalization. In realistic deployments, routers also verify that a proposed certificate is correctly witnessed.

Definition 25 (Soundness and completeness of a router).

Fix the ordered trigger family (χj)(\chi_{j}) and extractors. A router is sound if accepting (j,W)(j,W) implies: jj is a genuine trigger label, W≠∅W\neq\emptyset, W⊆𝒯⁡(E)W\subseteq\mathcal{T}(E), E⊧WχjE\models_{W}\chi_{j}, E⊧χjE\models\chi_{j}, and jj is the highest-priority satisfied trigger on the full event. It is complete if it accepts the canonical certificate of that selected trigger whenever the event is non-social and the extractor meets its contract. A certificate for a satisfied but unselected lower-priority trigger need not be accepted. Numerical execution is governed separately by Section 4.4.

Remark 7 (Why Theorem 8 is the right “normal form” statement).

Theorem 8 isolates the semantic projection induced by enforcing nonempty, token-sound witnessing: once empty-witness steps are rejected, the only behavior that survives enforcement is the behavior of the evidence-gated projection EG⁡(Pi)\mathrm{EG}(P_{i}). For full routers the same equality additionally needs selected-branch completeness. A sound but incomplete router may replace further evidence-bearing transitions by fallback.

8.5.1 A router class and semantic projection

We now lift the single “nonempty-witness” gate to an abstract class of routers and show that evidence-gating is a semantic projection induced by enforcement. The key point is that, once a router rejects unauditable (empty-witness) justifications and is complete on selected non-social satisfied triggers, any trigger protocol behaves exactly like its explicit evidence-gated compilation.

Router-enforced one-step semantics.

Recall that a witnessed protocol/contract XX determines (i) a one-step update map FX​(b,E)F_{X}(b,E) and (ii) a certificate map πX​(E)=(ℓ,W)\pi_{X}(E)=(\ell,W); canonicalization can\mathrm{can} is defined in Definition 20. We treat routers as accept/reject predicates over canonicalized certificates.

Definition 26 (Router acceptance predicate and enforced semantics).

A (deterministic) router is a predicate

𝖠𝖼𝖼:𝖤𝗏𝗍×({1,…,ri}∪{⊥})×𝒫⁡(𝒯)→{0,1},\mathsf{Acc}:\;\mathsf{Evt}\times(\{1,\dots,r_{i}\}\cup\{\bot\})\times\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{T})\ \to\ \{0,1\},

where 𝖠𝖼𝖼⁡(E,ℓ,W)=1\mathsf{Acc}(E,\ell,W)=1 means “accept the step justified by label ℓ\ell with witness WW on event EE.”

Given a witnessed protocol/contract XX with fallback δi\delta_{i} and certificate map πX​(E)\pi_{X}(E), define the router-enforced one-step update:

FX𝖠𝖼𝖼​(b,E):={FX​(b,E),𝖠𝖼𝖼⁡(E,can⁡(πX​(E)))=1,δi​(b,E),𝖠𝖼𝖼⁡(E,can⁡(πX​(E)))=0.F_{X}^{\mathsf{Acc}}(b,E)\;:=\;\begin{cases}F_{X}(b,E),&\mathsf{Acc}\big(E,\mathrm{can}(\pi_{X}(E))\big)=1,\\ \delta_{i}(b,E),&\mathsf{Acc}\big(E,\mathrm{can}(\pi_{X}(E))\big)=0.\end{cases}

The nonempty-witness gate of Definition 23 is the special case

𝖠𝖼𝖼(E,ℓ,W)=𝕀[ℓ∈{1,…,ri}∧W≠∅].\mathsf{Acc}(E,\ell,W)\;=\;\mathbb{I}\big[\ell\in\{1,\ldots,r_{i}\}\ \land\ W\neq\emptyset\big].
A router class.

We formalize the minimal router axioms needed for “semantic projection to evidence-gating.” These axioms are parameterized by a trigger family (χj)(\chi_{j}) and corresponding witness extractors Witχj\mathrm{Wit}_{\chi_{j}}.

Definition 27 (Axioms for a sound-and-complete router class).

Fix the ordered trigger family (χj)(\chi_{j}) and extractors satisfying Definition 18. The class ℜ⁡(χ,Wit)\mathfrak{R}(\chi,\mathrm{Wit}) consists of acceptance predicates with:

  1. 1.

    Malformed/empty rejection: reject every certificate with an invalid or fallback label, or with W=∅W=\emptyset.

  2. 2.

    Soundness: acceptance of (j,W)(j,W) implies nonempty validated membership, restricted and full-event satisfaction, and correct priority selection as in Definition 25.

  3. 3.

    Selected-branch completeness: when J⁡(E)≠∅J(E)\neq\emptyset, j=min≺iJ(E)j=\min_{\prec_{i}}J(E), and 𝒯⁡(E)≠∅\mathcal{T}(E)\neq\emptyset, accept (j,Witχj​(E))(j,\mathrm{Wit}_{\chi_{j}}(E)).

These axioms concern certificates generated from the same fixed contract and public context. For the numerical equalities below, the router computes or verifies the stated update.

Definition 28 (Sound routers and token-determinedness).

With (χj)(\chi_{j}) and Witχj\mathrm{Wit}_{\chi_{j}} fixed, write 𝖠𝖼𝖼∈ℜsnd​(χ,Wit)\mathsf{Acc}\in\mathfrak{R}_{\mathrm{snd}}(\chi,\mathrm{Wit}) if 𝖠𝖼𝖼\mathsf{Acc} satisfies the empty rejection and soundness clauses of Definition 27 (but not necessarily completeness).

We also say that 𝖠𝖼𝖼\mathsf{Acc} is token-determined if for all token-equivalent events E≡𝒯E′E\equiv_{\mathcal{T}}E^{\prime} and all certificates (ℓ,W)(\ell,W) with W⊆𝒯⁡(E)=𝒯⁡(E′)W\subseteq\mathcal{T}(E)=\mathcal{T}(E^{\prime}),

𝖠𝖼𝖼⁡(E,ℓ,W)=𝖠𝖼𝖼⁡(E′,ℓ,W).\mathsf{Acc}(E,\ell,W)=\mathsf{Acc}(E^{\prime},\ell,W).
Safety–liveness separation.

The next proposition makes precise a commonly used engineering heuristic: sound-but-incomplete routers preserve safety properties but may harm liveness (by rejecting admissible evidence-bearing updates).

Proposition 1 (Safety–liveness separation for routers).

Let XX be any witnessed trigger protocol or contract with fallback δi\delta_{i}, and let 𝖠𝖼𝖼∈ℜsnd​(χ,Wit)\mathsf{Acc}\in\mathfrak{R}_{\mathrm{snd}}(\chi,\mathrm{Wit}) be any sound router that rejects empty-witness certificates. Then every accepted non-fallback step of FX𝖠𝖼𝖼F_{X}^{\mathsf{Acc}} is admissible (in the sense that it is supported by a token-sound witness for the named trigger), while any rejected step devolves to fallback. Consequently, PBRC safety guarantees that are proved under the assumption “either a trigger update is admissible and evidence-witnessed or else fallback is applied” remain valid under sound-but-incomplete routers; completeness is only needed for liveness (eventual acceptance of admissible evidence-bearing steps) and for equivalence results that require that all admissible steps are accepted.

Proof.

By Definition 26, if the router rejects then the enforced semantics applies fallback. If the router accepts, then by soundness (Definition 27) the accepted certificate (j,W)(j,W) satisfies W⊆𝒯⁡(E)W\subseteq\mathcal{T}(E) and WW witnesses E⊧χjE\models\chi_{j}, i.e., the step is evidence-justified in the intended sense. Safety results that rely only on (i) fallback behavior and (ii) the fact that non-fallback steps are evidence-witnessed therefore continue to hold; completeness affects only whether admissible steps are eventually accepted. ∎

Evidence-gating as an idempotent projection.
Proposition 2 (Idempotence of evidence gating).

For any trigger protocol PiP_{i}, EG⁡(EG⁡(Pi))=EG⁡(Pi)\mathrm{EG}(\mathrm{EG}(P_{i}))=\mathrm{EG}(P_{i}) up to logical equivalence of triggers. Moreover, if PiP_{i} is already evidence-gated (i.e., every trigger ψi,j\psi_{i,j} implies ¬SocialOnly\neg\mathrm{SocialOnly}), then EG⁡(Pi)=Pi\mathrm{EG}(P_{i})=P_{i} (up to logical equivalence of triggers).

Proof.

By Definition 24, EG\mathrm{EG} conjoins ¬SocialOnly\neg\mathrm{SocialOnly} to every trigger. Conjoining the same conjunct twice is idempotent, hence EG⁡(EG⁡(Pi))=EG⁡(Pi)\mathrm{EG}(\mathrm{EG}(P_{i}))=\mathrm{EG}(P_{i}). If each ψi,j\psi_{i,j} already implies ¬SocialOnly\neg\mathrm{SocialOnly}, then ψi,j∧¬SocialOnly\psi_{i,j}\land\neg\mathrm{SocialOnly} is logically equivalent to ψi,j\psi_{i,j}, so the compilation does not change the trigger satisfaction relation and yields the same protocol/contract (up to propositional equivalence). ∎

Semantic projection theorem.

We now state the router-class normal form: any protocol, when enforced by a router in ℜ\mathfrak{R}, behaves exactly like its explicit evidence-gated compilation.

Theorem 9 (Router-class normal form (semantic projection to evidence gating)).

Let Pi=⟨(ψi,1,Vi,1),…,(ψi,ri,Vi,ri),≺i,δi⟩P_{i}=\langle(\psi_{i,1},V_{i,1}),\dots,(\psi_{i,r_{i}},V_{i,r_{i}}),\prec_{i},\delta_{i}\rangle be a witnessed trigger protocol whose witness extractors satisfy Definition 18. Let 𝖠𝖼𝖼∈ℜ⁡(ψ,Wit)\mathsf{Acc}\in\mathfrak{R}(\psi,\mathrm{Wit}) be any router that is sound, complete on selected non-social satisfaction, and rejects empty-witness certificates for the triggers (ψi,j)(\psi_{i,j}). Then for all beliefs bb and events EE,

FPi𝖠𝖼𝖼​(b,E)=FEG⁡(Pi)​(b,E).F_{P_{i}}^{\mathsf{Acc}}(b,E)\;=\;F_{\mathrm{EG}(P_{i})}(b,E).

In particular, under such enforcement, the externally observed behavior of PiP_{i} depends only on its evidence-gated projection EG⁡(Pi)\mathrm{EG}(P_{i}), not on any social-only trigger structure.

Proof.

Fix bb and EE.

Case 1: SocialOnly⁡(E)\mathrm{SocialOnly}(E). Then 𝒯⁡(E)=∅\mathcal{T}(E)=\emptyset. By token soundness (Definition 18), every extracted witness set is empty, hence can⁡(πPi​(E))=(⊥,∅)\mathrm{can}(\pi_{P_{i}}(E))=(\bot,\emptyset) (either because no trigger holds or because any selected trigger has empty witness and is canonicalized). By empty rejection, 𝖠𝖼𝖼⁡(E,⊥,∅)=0\mathsf{Acc}(E,\bot,\emptyset)=0, and Definition 26 yields

FPi𝖠𝖼𝖼​(b,E)=δi​(b,E).F_{P_{i}}^{\mathsf{Acc}}(b,E)=\delta_{i}(b,E).

In EG⁡(Pi)\mathrm{EG}(P_{i}), each trigger includes the conjunct ¬SocialOnly\neg\mathrm{SocialOnly}, which is false here, so no trigger is satisfied and

FEG⁡(Pi)​(b,E)=δi​(b,E).F_{\mathrm{EG}(P_{i})}(b,E)=\delta_{i}(b,E).

Thus the equality holds.

Case 2: ¬SocialOnly⁡(E)\neg\mathrm{SocialOnly}(E). Then for each jj, E⊧(ψi,j∧¬SocialOnly)E\models(\psi_{i,j}\land\neg\mathrm{SocialOnly}) iff E⊧ψi,jE\models\psi_{i,j}, so PiP_{i} and EG⁡(Pi)\mathrm{EG}(P_{i}) select the same highest-priority trigger label when any trigger is satisfied.

If JPi​(E)=∅J_{P_{i}}(E)=\emptyset, then both apply fallback δi​(b,E)\delta_{i}(b,E) and the equality is immediate.

If JPi​(E)≠∅J_{P_{i}}(E)\neq\emptyset, let j⋆=jPi⋆​(E)j^{\star}=j^{\star}_{P_{i}}(E). Since E⊧ψi,j⋆E\models\psi_{i,j^{\star}} and ¬SocialOnly⁡(E)\neg\mathrm{SocialOnly}(E), non-vacuity implies Witψi,j⋆​(E)≠∅\mathrm{Wit}_{\psi_{i,j^{\star}}}(E)\neq\emptyset. By completeness,

𝖠𝖼𝖼⁡(E,j⋆,Witψi,j⋆​(E))=1.\mathsf{Acc}\big(E,j^{\star},\mathrm{Wit}_{\psi_{i,j^{\star}}}(E)\big)=1.

Hence the router accepts the canonicalized certificate, and Definition 26 yields

FPi𝖠𝖼𝖼​(b,E)=FPi​(b,E)=Vi,j⋆​(b,E).F_{P_{i}}^{\mathsf{Acc}}(b,E)=F_{P_{i}}(b,E)=V_{i,j^{\star}}(b,E).

The evidence-gated contract EG⁡(Pi)\mathrm{EG}(P_{i}) applies the same operator Vi,j⋆V_{i,j^{\star}} on this event, so FEG⁡(Pi)​(b,E)=Vi,j⋆​(b,E)F_{\mathrm{EG}(P_{i})}(b,E)=V_{i,j^{\star}}(b,E), proving equality. ∎

Corollary 3 (Router transparency for evidence-gated contracts).

Let 𝖠𝖼𝖼∈ℜ⁡(χ,Wit)\mathsf{Acc}\in\mathfrak{R}(\chi,\mathrm{Wit}) and let CiC_{i} be an evidential contract whose triggers are of the form χj∧¬SocialOnly\chi_{j}\land\neg\mathrm{SocialOnly}, equipped with witness extractors satisfying Definition 18. Then

FCi𝖠𝖼𝖼​(b,E)=FCi​(b,E)for all ​b,E.F_{C_{i}}^{\mathsf{Acc}}(b,E)=F_{C_{i}}(b,E)\quad\text{for all }b,E.
Proof.

Fix b,Eb,E. If no trigger fires, then FCi​(b,E)=δi​(b,E)F_{C_{i}}(b,E)=\delta_{i}(b,E) and the certificate canonicalizes to (⊥,∅)(\bot,\emptyset), so the enforced semantics also yields δi​(b,E)\delta_{i}(b,E). If a trigger jj fires, evidentiality implies ¬SocialOnly⁡(E)\neg\mathrm{SocialOnly}(E); by non-vacuity the extracted witness is nonempty, and by completeness the router accepts the corresponding certificate. Hence FCi𝖠𝖼𝖼​(b,E)=FCi​(b,E)F_{C_{i}}^{\mathsf{Acc}}(b,E)=F_{C_{i}}(b,E). ∎

8.5.2 Token-sufficiency and persuasion separation

Router-level enforcement projects protocols onto evidence-gated dynamics (Theorems 8–9). The next result sharpens this into a separation principle: under natural invariance assumptions, the validated token set carried by an event is a sufficient statistic for the enforced update. Consequently, altering rhetoric, prestige cues, confidence posturing, or majority claims—without changing validated tokens—cannot affect accepted belief change.

Token-equivalence and token invariance.

We make explicit which components of a contract (and which enforcement mechanisms) are allowed to depend on non-token features of an event.

Definition 29 (Token-equivalence and token invariance).

Two events EE and E′E^{\prime} are token-equivalent, written E≡𝒯E′E\equiv_{\mathcal{T}}E^{\prime}, if they carry the same valid-token set:

E≡𝒯E′:⇔𝒯(E)=𝒯(E′).E\equiv_{\mathcal{T}}E^{\prime}\quad:\iff\quad\mathcal{T}(E)=\mathcal{T}(E^{\prime}).

A trigger χ\chi is token-invariant if E≡𝒯E′E\equiv_{\mathcal{T}}E^{\prime} implies

(E⊧χ)⟺(E′⊧χ).(E\models\chi)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ (E^{\prime}\models\chi).

An operator UU (including fallback) is token-invariant if E≡𝒯E′E\equiv_{\mathcal{T}}E^{\prime} implies

U⁡(b,E)=U⁡(b,E′)for all beliefs ​b∈Δ⁡(ℋ).U(b,E)=U(b,E^{\prime})\qquad\text{for all beliefs }b\in\Delta(\mathcal{H}).

A witness extractor Witχ\mathrm{Wit}_{\chi} is token-invariant if E≡𝒯E′E\equiv_{\mathcal{T}}E^{\prime} implies

Witχ​(E)=Witχ​(E′).\mathrm{Wit}_{\chi}(E)=\mathrm{Wit}_{\chi}(E^{\prime}).
Remark 8 (Scope of invariance).

Token-invariance is a design constraint, not a meta-theorem: it formalizes that admissibility is intended to depend on validated evidence, not on who said what or how it was phrased. If a deployment wants to treat source identity or reputation as admissible input, then that information should be encoded as (and validated as) tokens; otherwise the system is vulnerable to purely social influence in exactly the sense PBRC is designed to exclude.

Token-sufficiency theorem.

We also need a mild invariance condition on the router: acceptance should not depend on non-token rhetoric when presented with the same canonicalized certificate and witness set. This is captured by token-determinedness (Definition 28).

Theorem 10 (Token-sufficiency (persuasion separation)).

Let CiC_{i} be an evidential contract whose triggers, operators (including fallback), and witness extractors are token-invariant (Definition 29). Let 𝖠𝖼𝖼∈ℜsnd​(χ,Wit)\mathsf{Acc}\in\mathfrak{R}_{\mathrm{snd}}(\chi,\mathrm{Wit}) be any sound router that is token-determined (Definition 28). Then for all beliefs bb and all token-equivalent events E≡𝒯E′E\equiv_{\mathcal{T}}E^{\prime},

FCi𝖠𝖼𝖼​(b,E)=FCi𝖠𝖼𝖼​(b,E′).F_{C_{i}}^{\mathsf{Acc}}(b,E)\;=\;F_{C_{i}}^{\mathsf{Acc}}(b,E^{\prime}).

In particular, changing unvalidated message content (rhetoric, confidence, sender identity, majority claims) without changing the set of valid evidence tokens cannot change any enforced belief update.

Proof.

Fix a belief bb and token-equivalent events E≡𝒯E′E\equiv_{\mathcal{T}}E^{\prime}, so 𝒯⁡(E)=𝒯⁡(E′)\mathcal{T}(E)=\mathcal{T}(E^{\prime}).

Let πCi​(E)=(ℓ,W)\pi_{C_{i}}(E)=(\ell,W) and πCi​(E′)=(ℓ′,W′)\pi_{C_{i}}(E^{\prime})=(\ell^{\prime},W^{\prime}) be the (uncanonicalized) certificates proposed by CiC_{i}. Because triggers are token-invariant, the set of satisfied triggers (and hence the selected highest-priority trigger label, or fallback) is the same on EE and E′E^{\prime}, so ℓ=ℓ′\ell=\ell^{\prime}. Because witness extractors are token-invariant, the extracted witness sets also coincide: W=W′W=W^{\prime}. Therefore the canonicalized certificates coincide:

can⁡(πCi​(E))=can⁡(πCi​(E′))=:(ℓ¯,W¯),with ​W¯⊆𝒯⁡(E)=𝒯⁡(E′).\mathrm{can}(\pi_{C_{i}}(E))=\mathrm{can}(\pi_{C_{i}}(E^{\prime}))=:(\bar{\ell},\bar{W}),\qquad\text{with }\bar{W}\subseteq\mathcal{T}(E)=\mathcal{T}(E^{\prime}).

By token-invariance of operators (including fallback), the candidate (ungated) update agrees:

FCi​(b,E)=FCi​(b,E′).F_{C_{i}}(b,E)=F_{C_{i}}(b,E^{\prime}).

Finally, by token-determinedness of the router and W¯⊆𝒯⁡(E)=𝒯⁡(E′)\bar{W}\subseteq\mathcal{T}(E)=\mathcal{T}(E^{\prime}), we have

𝖠𝖼𝖼⁡(E,ℓ¯,W¯)=𝖠𝖼𝖼⁡(E′,ℓ¯,W¯).\mathsf{Acc}(E,\bar{\ell},\bar{W})=\mathsf{Acc}(E^{\prime},\bar{\ell},\bar{W}).

Applying the enforced semantics (Definition 26) yields the same accept/reject decision and the same resulting update on EE and E′E^{\prime}, hence FCi𝖠𝖼𝖼​(b,E)=FCi𝖠𝖼𝖼​(b,E′)F_{C_{i}}^{\mathsf{Acc}}(b,E)=F_{C_{i}}^{\mathsf{Acc}}(b,E^{\prime}). ∎

A counterexample without token invariance.

The next proposition records that token-invariance is not a cosmetic restriction: if a trigger (or witness extractor) is allowed to depend on non-token features (e.g., sender identity), then token-sufficiency can fail even with sound enforcement.

Proposition 3 (Token-sufficiency can fail without token invariance).

Token-invariance in Theorem 10 is essential. Concretely, there exists an evidential contract CC and a sound-and-complete router such that for some belief bb there are token-equivalent events E≡𝒯E′E\equiv_{\mathcal{T}}E^{\prime} with

FC𝖠𝖼𝖼​(b,E)≠FC𝖠𝖼𝖼​(b,E′).F_{C}^{\mathsf{Acc}}(b,E)\neq F_{C}^{\mathsf{Acc}}(b,E^{\prime}).
Proof.

Let ℋ={h0,h1}\mathcal{H}=\{h_{0},h_{1}\} and fix a token τ⋆\tau^{\star} with Valid⁡(τ⋆)\mathrm{Valid}(\tau^{\star}) and Supports⁡(τ⋆,h1)\mathrm{Supports}(\tau^{\star},h_{1}). Define a sender-sensitive (hence not token-invariant) trigger:

ψ:=∃m​∃τ⁡(Send⁡(a0,i,m,t)∧HasTok⁡(m,τ)∧Valid⁡(τ)),\psi\;:=\;\exists m\,\exists\tau\ \Big(\mathrm{Send}(a_{0},i,m,t)\ \wedge\ \mathrm{HasTok}(m,\tau)\ \wedge\ \mathrm{Valid}(\tau)\Big),

i.e., “agent ii received a valid token from distinguished sender a0a_{0}.”

Let CC have a single trigger ψ\psi with an operator that shifts probability mass toward h1h_{1} (e.g., a bounded log-odds increase for h1h_{1}), and let fallback be any argmax-preserving operator (e.g., identity or skeptical dilution). The contract is evidential because ψ\psi implies ¬SocialOnly\neg\mathrm{SocialOnly} (it explicitly requires a valid token).

Construct two events EE and E′E^{\prime} that contain the same valid token set 𝒯⁡(E)=𝒯⁡(E′)={τ⋆}\mathcal{T}(E)=\mathcal{T}(E^{\prime})=\{\tau^{\star}\}, but differ only in sender metadata: in EE the message carrying τ⋆\tau^{\star} is sent by a0a_{0}, while in E′E^{\prime} it is sent by some a1≠a0a_{1}\neq a_{0}. Then E≡𝒯E′E\equiv_{\mathcal{T}}E^{\prime}, but E⊧ψE\models\psi whereas E′⊧̸ψE^{\prime}\not\models\psi. Therefore CC applies the trigger operator on EE and fallback on E′E^{\prime}, yielding different one-step updates. A sound-and-complete router accepts the evidence-bearing step on EE and (trivially) enforces fallback on E′E^{\prime}, so FC𝖠𝖼𝖼​(b,E)≠FC𝖠𝖼𝖼​(b,E′)F_{C}^{\mathsf{Acc}}(b,E)\neq F_{C}^{\mathsf{Acc}}(b,E^{\prime}) for any belief bb on which the trigger operator differs from fallback. ∎

8.5.3 Token exposure traces and network-level invariance

The token-sufficiency theorem (Theorem 10) is a one-step, single-agent statement: under token-invariant contracts and token-determined enforcement, an agent’s enforced update depends on an event only through its validated token set. We now lift this to multi-agent runs. The key observation is that, once contracts and routers satisfy the same invariance discipline, the entire enforced belief trajectory of each agent is determined by the sequence of token sets it is exposed to over time. We formalize this as a token exposure trace and show that token-trace equivalence implies equality of enforced belief trajectories.

Definition 30 (Token exposure trace and token-trace equivalence).

Fix a horizon T∈ℕT\in\mathbb{N}. For an agent ii with received events Ei0,…,EiT−1E_{i}^{0},\dots,E_{i}^{T-1}, define its token exposure trace up to TT as

Trace𝒯T​(i):=(𝒯⁡(Ei0),𝒯⁡(Ei1),…,𝒯⁡(EiT−1)).\mathrm{Trace}^{T}_{\mathcal{T}}(i)\;:=\;\big(\mathcal{T}(E_{i}^{0}),\mathcal{T}(E_{i}^{1}),\dots,\mathcal{T}(E_{i}^{T-1})\big).

Two deliberation runs ρ\rho and ρ′\rho^{\prime} are token-trace equivalent up to TT, written ρ≡Ttraceρ′\rho\equiv^{T}_{\mathrm{trace}}\rho^{\prime}, if for every agent i∈𝒜i\in\mathcal{A} and every round t<Tt<T,

𝒯⁡(Ei,ρt)=𝒯⁡(Ei,ρ′t).\mathcal{T}(E_{i,\rho}^{t})=\mathcal{T}(E_{i,\rho^{\prime}}^{t}).
Theorem 11 (Token exposure traces determine enforced belief trajectories).

Assume each agent ii runs an evidential contract CiC_{i} whose triggers, operators (including fallback), and witness extractors are token-invariant (Definition 29), and is enforced by a router 𝖠𝖼𝖼i\mathsf{Acc}_{i} that is sound and token-determined (Definition 28).33 3 Equivalently, 𝖠𝖼𝖼i∈ℜsnd​(χ,Wit)\mathsf{Acc}_{i}\in\mathfrak{R}_{\mathrm{snd}}(\chi,\mathrm{Wit}) and is token-determined. Completeness is not required for this invariance statement. Consider two runs ρ\rho and ρ′\rho^{\prime} with identical initial beliefs bi,ρ0=bi,ρ′0b_{i,\rho}^{0}=b_{i,\rho^{\prime}}^{0} for all ii. If ρ≡Ttraceρ′\rho\equiv^{T}_{\mathrm{trace}}\rho^{\prime}, then for all agents i∈𝒜i\in\mathcal{A} and all rounds t≤Tt\leq T,

bi,ρt=bi,ρ′t.b_{i,\rho}^{t}\;=\;b_{i,\rho^{\prime}}^{t}.

In particular, the enforced terminal beliefs at horizon TT are identical across runs.

Proof.

We prove by induction on t∈{0,1,…,T}t\in\{0,1,\dots,T\} that bi,ρt=bi,ρ′tb_{i,\rho}^{t}=b_{i,\rho^{\prime}}^{t} for all agents ii.

Base case (t=0t=0). Holds by hypothesis.

Inductive step. Fix t<Tt<T and assume bi,ρt=bi,ρ′tb_{i,\rho}^{t}=b_{i,\rho^{\prime}}^{t} for all ii. By token-trace equivalence, for each agent ii we have

𝒯⁡(Ei,ρt)=𝒯⁡(Ei,ρ′t),\mathcal{T}(E_{i,\rho}^{t})=\mathcal{T}(E_{i,\rho^{\prime}}^{t}),

i.e., Ei,ρt≡𝒯Ei,ρ′tE_{i,\rho}^{t}\equiv_{\mathcal{T}}E_{i,\rho^{\prime}}^{t}. Apply Theorem 10 to agent ii with belief b=bi,ρt=bi,ρ′tb=b_{i,\rho}^{t}=b_{i,\rho^{\prime}}^{t} and token-equivalent events E=Ei,ρtE=E_{i,\rho}^{t}, E′=Ei,ρ′tE^{\prime}=E_{i,\rho^{\prime}}^{t} to obtain

FCi𝖠𝖼𝖼i​(bi,ρt,Ei,ρt)=FCi𝖠𝖼𝖼i​(bi,ρ′t,Ei,ρ′t).F_{C_{i}}^{\mathsf{Acc}_{i}}(b_{i,\rho}^{t},E_{i,\rho}^{t})=F_{C_{i}}^{\mathsf{Acc}_{i}}(b_{i,\rho^{\prime}}^{t},E_{i,\rho^{\prime}}^{t}).

By definition of the run semantics, the left-hand side is bi,ρt+1b_{i,\rho}^{t+1} and the right-hand side is bi,ρ′t+1b_{i,\rho^{\prime}}^{t+1}. Thus bi,ρt+1=bi,ρ′t+1b_{i,\rho}^{t+1}=b_{i,\rho^{\prime}}^{t+1} for each ii, completing the induction. ∎

Corollary 4 (Topology and rhetoric are irrelevant given token traces).

Under the hypotheses of Theorem 11, any two multi-agent deliberation runs (possibly with different network topology, message ordering, and rhetorical content) that induce the same token exposure traces up to horizon TT induce identical enforced belief trajectories up to TT.

8.5.4 Topology-to-trace structural conditions under token flooding

Theorems 10 and 11 reduce dependence, with contracts, public context, and initial states fixed, on the communication structure to a single question: which validated tokens reach which agents at which times. We now give a closed-form characterization of token exposure traces under a minimal dissemination layer: token flooding, where agents forward validated tokens verbatim along the communication graph.

Definition 31 (Communication graph and flooding).

Fix a directed communication graph G=(𝒜,ℰ)G=(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{E}). Write InG​(i):={j∈𝒜:(j,i)∈ℰ}\mathrm{In}_{G}(i):=\{j\in\mathcal{A}:(j,i)\in\mathcal{E}\}. Let 𝒦it⊆𝒯\mathcal{K}_{i}^{t}\subseteq\mathcal{T} denote the valid tokens known immediately before round tt, after tt delivery rounds. Thus 𝒦i0\mathcal{K}_{i}^{0} is initial knowledge, and EitE_{i}^{t} is delivered during round tt. Assume an initial placement (𝒦i0)i∈𝒜(\mathcal{K}_{i}^{0})_{i\in\mathcal{A}}.

Flooding is the dissemination rule: at each round t≥0t\geq 0, each agent jj sends a message containing all tokens in 𝒦jt\mathcal{K}_{j}^{t} to every out-neighbor. Agent ii receives the event EitE_{i}^{t} consisting of those messages, so

𝒯⁡(Eit)=⋃j∈InG​(i)𝒦jt,𝒦it+1=𝒦it∪𝒯⁡(Eit).\mathcal{T}(E_{i}^{t})=\bigcup_{j\in\mathrm{In}_{G}(i)}\mathcal{K}_{j}^{t},\qquad\mathcal{K}_{i}^{t+1}=\mathcal{K}_{i}^{t}\cup\mathcal{T}(E_{i}^{t}).

We assume reliable synchronous delivery, fixed token validity and annotations, and no exogenous births or expiry over the stated horizon. Self-loops are allowed and represent explicit self-delivery; local retention alone is not an incoming message. Exogenous births or time-varying validity require an augmented model and are not covered by these identities.

Let distG​(u,v)∈ℕ∪{∞}\mathrm{dist}_{G}(u,v)\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\} be the length of the shortest directed path from uu to vv in GG, and ∞\infty if none exists. Define the directed diameter, with value ∞\infty for a graph that is not strongly connected, by

D⁡(G):=maxu,v∈𝒜⁡distG​(u,v).D(G):=\max_{u,v\in\mathcal{A}}\mathrm{dist}_{G}(u,v).
Remark 9 (Standard flooding facts vs. PBRC-specific use).

Distance/diameter characterizations of flooding are classical in distributed algorithms (e.g., [Lynch(1996)]). Our use here is to compose these structural facts with PBRC’s token-sufficiency and enforcement semantics to obtain end-to-end invariance statements.

Theorem 12 (Knowledge and incoming exposure under flooding).

Let PG≤sP_{G}^{\leq s} be the relation of positive-length directed walks of lengths 1,…,s1,\ldots,s; set PG≤0=∅P_{G}^{\leq 0}=\emptyset. Under Definition 31, for every ii and t≥0t\geq 0,

𝒦it=⋃u:distG​(u,i)≤t𝒦u0,𝒯(Eit)=⋃u:(u,i)∈PG≤t+1𝒦u0.\mathcal{K}_{i}^{t}=\bigcup_{u:\,\mathrm{dist}_{G}(u,i)\leq t}\mathcal{K}_{u}^{0},\qquad\mathcal{T}(E_{i}^{t})=\bigcup_{u:\,(u,i)\in P_{G}^{\leq t+1}}\mathcal{K}_{u}^{0}.

The first union concerns retained knowledge; the second concerns actual incoming messages.

Proof.

At t=0t=0, distance zero selects only the node itself. If the knowledge identity holds at tt, the recurrence adds the knowledge of every predecessor. A path of length at most t+1t+1 either already has length at most tt or has a last edge from a predecessor reached within tt steps. This proves the knowledge identity by induction. For the incoming event, substitute that identity:

𝒯(Eit)=⋃j:(j,i)∈ℰ⋃u:distG​(u,j)≤t𝒦u0.\mathcal{T}(E_{i}^{t})=\bigcup_{j:(j,i)\in\mathcal{E}}\ \bigcup_{u:\mathrm{dist}_{G}(u,j)\leq t}\mathcal{K}_{u}^{0}.

A source belongs to this union exactly when it reaches a predecessor within tt steps. Appending the final edge gives a walk of positive length at most t+1t+1 into ii. Conversely, the prefix of such a walk reaches a predecessor within distance at most tt. This proves the exposure identity, including returning walks with u=iu=i. ∎

Example 2 (Local knowledge is not an incoming exposure).

An isolated node with 𝒦i0={τ}\mathcal{K}_{i}^{0}=\{\tau\} retains τ\tau at every time, but its incoming event is empty. The zero-length path from ii to itself cannot deliver a message. If a deployment explicitly adds retained local tokens to the event, the enlarged exposure instead equals 𝒦it+1\mathcal{K}_{i}^{t+1}; that is a different, self-inclusive event convention.

Corollary 5 (Diameter bound for evidence closure under flooding).

If GG is strongly connected with diameter D⁡(G)<∞D(G)<\infty, then for every agent ii,

𝒦iD⁡(G)=⋃j∈𝒜𝒦j0.\mathcal{K}_{i}^{D(G)}=\bigcup_{j\in\mathcal{A}}\mathcal{K}_{j}^{0}.

After D⁡(G)D(G) delivery rounds every agent possesses all initial tokens. A token initially local to an agent need not have been received back through an incoming edge.

Proof.

If GG is strongly connected, then distG​(j,i)≤D⁡(G)\mathrm{dist}_{G}(j,i)\leq D(G) for all j,ij,i. Apply Theorem 12 at time t=D⁡(G)t=D(G). ∎

Definition 32 (Truncated incoming-reachability equivalence).

For a horizon T∈ℕT\in\mathbb{N}, graphs on the same vertices are TT-incoming-reachability equivalent if

PG≤s=PG′≤sfor ​s=1,…,T.P_{G}^{\leq s}=P_{G^{\prime}}^{\leq s}\qquad\text{for }s=1,\ldots,T.

This uses positive-length walks rather than the reflexive distance relation. For T≥1T\geq 1, PG≤1=ℰP_{G}^{\leq 1}=\mathcal{E}, so universal equivalence already entails identical adjacency, including self-loops. Equality of exposure traces for a particular non-distinguishing token placement can be weaker.

Theorem 13 (Incoming-reachability implies exposure-trace equivalence).

Assume flooding on G,G′G,G^{\prime} with identical initial token placement and fixed common context. If they are TT-incoming-reachability equivalent, their events satisfy ρG≡TtraceρG′\rho_{G}\equiv^{T}_{\rm trace}\rho_{G^{\prime}}. Under the hypotheses of Theorem 11, identical initial beliefs then yield identical enforced trajectories through time TT.

Proof.

For every t<Tt<T and ii, Theorem 12 expresses the exposure as the union of 𝒦u0\mathcal{K}_{u}^{0} over (u,i)∈PG≤t+1(u,i)\in P_{G}^{\leq t+1}. The relations and initial placement coincide, so the two unions coincide. Apply Theorem 11. ∎

Proposition 4 (Monotonicity under edge addition).

Assume flooding with a fixed initial placement (𝒦i0)i∈𝒜(\mathcal{K}_{i}^{0})_{i\in\mathcal{A}}. If G′=(𝒜,ℰ′)G^{\prime}=(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{E}^{\prime}) satisfies ℰ⊆ℰ′\mathcal{E}\subseteq\mathcal{E}^{\prime} (i.e., G′G^{\prime} adds edges), then for all agents ii and all rounds tt,

𝒦i,Gt⊆𝒦i,G′tand𝒯⁡(Ei,Gt)⊆𝒯⁡(Ei,G′t).\mathcal{K}_{i,G}^{t}\subseteq\mathcal{K}_{i,G^{\prime}}^{t}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\mathcal{T}(E_{i,G}^{t})\subseteq\mathcal{T}(E_{i,G^{\prime}}^{t}).
Proof.

Adding edges can only weakly decrease directed distances: distG′​(u,v)≤distG​(u,v)\mathrm{dist}_{G^{\prime}}(u,v)\leq\mathrm{dist}_{G}(u,v) for all u,vu,v. Apply Theorem 12 to both graphs: the set of sources within distance ≤t\leq t in GG is contained in the corresponding set for G′G^{\prime}, hence 𝒦i,Gt⊆𝒦i,G′t\mathcal{K}_{i,G}^{t}\subseteq\mathcal{K}_{i,G^{\prime}}^{t}. Every positive-length walk in GG is also a walk in G′G^{\prime}, so PG≤t+1⊆PG′≤t+1P_{G}^{\leq t+1}\subseteq P_{G^{\prime}}^{\leq t+1}. The exposure inclusion follows from the second identity of Theorem 12. This does not assert monotonicity of accuracy or confidence as edges are added. ∎

Tightness and optimality.

The distance characterization above is not merely descriptive; it is optimal among all dissemination layers that respect the communication graph by allowing tokens to traverse at most one edge per round.

Definition 33 (Edge-respecting token dissemination).

Fix a directed graph G=(𝒜,ℰ)G=(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{E}) and an initial placement (𝒦i0)i∈𝒜(\mathcal{K}_{i}^{0})_{i\in\mathcal{A}}. A dissemination layer is edge-respecting if it produces token knowledge sets (𝒦it)i∈𝒜,t≥0(\mathcal{K}_{i}^{t})_{i\in\mathcal{A},t\geq 0} such that for every t≥0t\geq 0 and every agent ii,

𝒦it+1⊆𝒦it∪⋃j∈InG​(i)𝒦jt.\mathcal{K}_{i}^{t+1}\ \subseteq\ \mathcal{K}_{i}^{t}\ \cup\ \bigcup_{j\in\mathrm{In}_{G}(i)}\mathcal{K}_{j}^{t}.

Equivalently, new tokens acquired at round t+1t+1 must come from in-neighbors’ knowledge at round tt (or be retained locally). Flooding is the special case where the inclusion holds with equality.

Lemma 5 (Distance lower bound for edge-respecting dissemination).

Under any edge-respecting dissemination on GG, for every agent ii and every t≥0t\geq 0,

𝒦it⊆⋃j∈𝒜:distG​(j,i)≤t𝒦j0.\mathcal{K}_{i}^{t}\ \subseteq\ \bigcup_{\begin{subarray}{c}j\in\mathcal{A}:\\ \mathrm{dist}_{G}(j,i)\leq t\end{subarray}}\mathcal{K}_{j}^{0}.
Proof.

By induction on tt.

Base (t=0t=0). Trivial.

Step. Assume the claim holds for tt. By Definition 33,

𝒦it+1⊆𝒦it∪⋃j∈InG​(i)𝒦jt.\mathcal{K}_{i}^{t+1}\subseteq\mathcal{K}_{i}^{t}\cup\bigcup_{j\in\mathrm{In}_{G}(i)}\mathcal{K}_{j}^{t}.

Apply the induction hypothesis to 𝒦it\mathcal{K}_{i}^{t} and each 𝒦jt\mathcal{K}_{j}^{t} and use the same one-edge extension argument as in the proof of Theorem 12 to conclude 𝒦it+1⊆⋃j:distG​(j,i)≤t+1𝒦j0\mathcal{K}_{i}^{t+1}\subseteq\bigcup_{j:\mathrm{dist}_{G}(j,i)\leq t+1}\mathcal{K}_{j}^{0}. ∎

Theorem 14 (Flooding is optimal (maximal token spread at every time)).

Fix GG and an initial placement. Let (𝒦it)𝖺𝗇𝗒(\mathcal{K}_{i}^{t})^{\mathsf{any}} be the knowledge sets produced by any edge-respecting dissemination (Definition 33) and let (𝒦it)𝖿𝗅𝗈𝗈𝖽(\mathcal{K}_{i}^{t})^{\mathsf{flood}} be the knowledge sets under flooding (Definition 31). Then for all agents ii and all rounds tt,

(𝒦it)𝖺𝗇𝗒⊆(𝒦it)𝖿𝗅𝗈𝗈𝖽.(\mathcal{K}_{i}^{t})^{\mathsf{any}}\ \subseteq\ (\mathcal{K}_{i}^{t})^{\mathsf{flood}}.

Consequently, flooding minimizes the worst-case time to universal evidence closure among all edge-respecting dissemination layers on GG.

Proof.

By Lemma 5,

(𝒦it)𝖺𝗇𝗒⊆⋃j:distG​(j,i)≤t𝒦j0.(\mathcal{K}_{i}^{t})^{\mathsf{any}}\subseteq\bigcup_{j:\mathrm{dist}_{G}(j,i)\leq t}\mathcal{K}_{j}^{0}.

By Theorem 12, the right-hand side equals (𝒦it)𝖿𝗅𝗈𝗈𝖽(\mathcal{K}_{i}^{t})^{\mathsf{flood}} under flooding. Thus (𝒦it)𝖺𝗇𝗒⊆(𝒦it)𝖿𝗅𝗈𝗈𝖽(\mathcal{K}_{i}^{t})^{\mathsf{any}}\subseteq(\mathcal{K}_{i}^{t})^{\mathsf{flood}} for all i,ti,t. The closure-time claim follows: if flooding has not delivered some initial token to some agent by time tt, then no edge-respecting protocol could have delivered it either. ∎

Corollary 6 (Tight diameter lower bound for universal closure).

Suppose a dissemination layer on GG is edge-respecting and the admissible placements include a valid token located at any single source. If it achieves universal evidence closure by time TT—i.e., for every initial placement and every agent ii,

𝒦iT=⋃j∈𝒜𝒦j0,\mathcal{K}_{i}^{T}=\bigcup_{j\in\mathcal{A}}\mathcal{K}_{j}^{0},

then necessarily D⁡(G)≤TD(G)\leq T (in particular, GG must be strongly connected). Conversely, if D⁡(G)≤TD(G)\leq T then flooding achieves universal closure by time TT. Thus, under edge-respecting dissemination, the minimum worst-case closure time is exactly the directed diameter D⁡(G)D(G).

Proof.

(Necessity.) If D⁡(G)>TD(G)>T, pick u,vu,v with distG​(u,v)>T\mathrm{dist}_{G}(u,v)>T. Consider an initial placement with a single unique token τ\tau placed at uu: τ∈𝒦u0\tau\in\mathcal{K}_{u}^{0} and τ∉𝒦j0\tau\notin\mathcal{K}_{j}^{0} for j≠uj\neq u. By Lemma 5, τ∉𝒦vT\tau\notin\mathcal{K}_{v}^{T}, contradicting universal closure.

(Sufficiency.) If D⁡(G)≤TD(G)\leq T, then for all j,ij,i we have distG​(j,i)≤T\mathrm{dist}_{G}(j,i)\leq T. By Corollary 5 (or directly by Theorem 12 with t=Tt=T), flooding yields 𝒦iT=⋃j𝒦j0\mathcal{K}_{i}^{T}=\bigcup_{j}\mathcal{K}_{j}^{0} for all ii. ∎

Theorem 15 (Universal exposure-trace characterization).

  1. 1.

    PG≤s=PG′≤sP_{G}^{\leq s}=P_{G^{\prime}}^{\leq s} for s=1,…,Ts=1,\ldots,T;

  3. 3.

    they agree for the placement 𝒦u0={τu}\mathcal{K}_{u}^{0}=\{\tau_{u}\}.

Proof.

Theorem 13 gives (1)⇒\Rightarrow(2); (2)⇒\Rightarrow(3) is immediate. For (3)⇒\Rightarrow(1), fix s∈{1,…,T}s\in\{1,\ldots,T\} and vertices u,vu,v. By the exposure identity,

τu∈𝒯(Ev,Gs−1)⟺(u,v)∈PG≤s.\tau_{u}\in\mathcal{T}(E_{v,G}^{s-1})\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(u,v)\in P_{G}^{\leq s}.

8.5.5 End-to-end factorization theorem

The preceding results compose when the transition rules, context schedule, and evidence semantics are fixed. Flooding determines incoming exposure through positive-length walks; the standard diameter bound determines retained knowledge closure.

Theorem 16 (End-to-end factorization of topology effects).

Fix initial beliefs, contracts, and a common public context schedule through horizon TT. Each agent runs PiP_{i} under a state-holding or operator-verifying router in ℜ⁡(ψi,Witi)\mathfrak{R}(\psi_{i},\mathrm{Wit}_{i}), with extractors satisfying Definition 18. Let Ci=EG⁡(Pi)C_{i}=\mathrm{EG}(P_{i}) inherit the extractors of PiP_{i} and have token-invariant triggers, operators (including fallback), and extractors. Under synchronous flooding with fixed validity/annotations and no exogenous births or expiry:

  1. 1.

    bitb_{i}^{t}, t≤Tt\leq T, is determined by the fixed transition rules/context, initial beliefs, initial token placement, and (PG≤s)1≤s≤t(P_{G}^{\leq s})_{1\leq s\leq t}. Changing unvalidated rhetoric while preserving those inputs does not change the enforced state.

  2. 2.

    Graphs with the same positive-walk relations through TT, initial beliefs, and token placement give identical belief trajectories through TT and identical canonical accepted certificates for rounds t<Tt<T.

  3. 3.

    Universal retained-token knowledge closure for all placements has minimum worst-case time D⁡(G)D(G) among edge-respecting dissemination layers, with infinite time if the graph is not strongly connected; assume the distinguishing token placements in Corollary 6 are allowed.

Proof.

Complete routing and Theorem 9 give

bit+1=FPi𝖠𝖼𝖼i​(bit,Eit)=FCi​(bit,Eit).b_{i}^{t+1}=F_{P_{i}}^{\mathsf{Acc}_{i}}(b_{i}^{t},E_{i}^{t})=F_{C_{i}}(b_{i}^{t},E_{i}^{t}).

For the fixed contract, token-invariant triggers select the same branch on token-equivalent events, and token-invariant operators give the same successor. Thus the last expression factors through 𝒯⁡(Eit)\mathcal{T}(E_{i}^{t}); no additional token-determinedness assumption on the acceptance of arbitrary certificates is needed because completeness has already removed router variation on the generated certificates. Theorem 12 determines this set from PG≤t+1P_{G}^{\leq t+1} and the initial placement. Induction on tt proves (1), and equality of these inputs proves belief equality in (2). The selected labels and inherited token-invariant witnesses also agree; completeness accepts these certificates on non-social selected steps, and otherwise both logs project to fallback. This proves the certificate part of (2). Item (3) is Corollary 6 and concerns knowledge, not return delivery of one’s own token. ∎

Figure 5 summarizes the dependency structure in Theorem 16: topology affects enforced beliefs through positive-walk relations and the induced token-exposure traces, with all other transition inputs fixed.

Remark 10 (Interpretation).

Theorem 16 formalizes a sharp contrast with conformity-driven failures: increasing connectivity can accelerate the propagation of validated evidence (tokens), but it cannot create epistemic pressure in the absence of evidence because social-only events are forced into fallback behavior under evidence-gated enforcement.

Gate transparency for compliant evidential contracts.

A crucial deployment requirement is that enforcement should not perturb agents that already follow an evidential PBRC contract.

Proposition 5 (Gate transparency).

Let CiC_{i} be an evidential PBRC contract and assume its witness extractors satisfy non-vacuity on non-social satisfaction (Definition 18). Then the nonempty-witness gate is transparent:

FCi𝗀𝖺𝗍𝖾​(b,E)=FCi​(b,E)for all ​b,E.F^{\mathsf{gate}}_{C_{i}}(b,E)=F_{C_{i}}(b,E)\quad\text{for all }b,E.
Proof.

If no trigger is satisfied, then FCi​(b,E)=δi​(b,E)F_{C_{i}}(b,E)=\delta_{i}(b,E) and πCi​(E)=(⊥,∅)\pi_{C_{i}}(E)=(\bot,\emptyset), so the gate outputs δi​(b,E)\delta_{i}(b,E) as well. If some trigger is satisfied, then evidentiality implies ¬SocialOnly⁡(E)\neg\mathrm{SocialOnly}(E), and by non-vacuity the witness is nonempty, hence can⁡(πCi​(E))≠(⊥,∅)\mathrm{can}(\pi_{C_{i}}(E))\neq(\bot,\emptyset) and the gate accepts FCi​(b,E)F_{C_{i}}(b,E). Thus the gated and ungated outputs coincide in all cases. ∎

Theorem 17 (Epistemic accountability).

Let CiC_{i} be an evidential PBRC contract with an argmax-preserving fallback δi\delta_{i}, and let the agent be enforced by a sound router that rejects empty-witness certificates and faithfully computes or verifies the numerical operator or fallback. Consider any run producing beliefs (bit)t≥0(b_{i}^{t})_{t\geq 0} and events (Eit)t≥0(E_{i}^{t})_{t\geq 0}. If argmax⁡(bit)≠argmax⁡(bi0)\mathrm{argmax}(b_{i}^{t})\neq\mathrm{argmax}(b_{i}^{0}) for some tt, then there exists a least index s<ts<t such that argmax⁡(bis+1)≠argmax⁡(bis)\mathrm{argmax}(b_{i}^{s+1})\neq\mathrm{argmax}(b_{i}^{s}), and this step is necessarily evidence-triggered: the router accepted a certificate πis=(j,W)\pi_{i}^{s}=(j,W) with W≠∅W\neq\emptyset and W⊆𝒯⁡(Eis)W\subseteq\mathcal{T}(E_{i}^{s}) witnessing Eis⊧φi,jE_{i}^{s}\models\varphi_{i,j}. In particular, a top-set change has a recorded nonempty certificate licensing its selected transition. Independence from rhetoric additionally requires token invariance; the certificate alone does not identify a sole causal token.

Proof.

Let ss be the smallest index such that argmax⁡(bis+1)≠argmax⁡(bis)\mathrm{argmax}(b_{i}^{s+1})\neq\mathrm{argmax}(b_{i}^{s}). Suppose for contradiction that the step ss was not evidence-triggered. Then either no trigger was satisfied (so fallback applies) or the router rejected the proposed step (including due to an empty-witness/invalid certificate), in which case enforcement forces fallback. In either case,

bis+1=δi​(bis,Eis).b_{i}^{s+1}=\delta_{i}(b_{i}^{s},E_{i}^{s}).

By argmax preservation of δi\delta_{i}, argmax⁡(bis+1)=argmax⁡(bis)\mathrm{argmax}(b_{i}^{s+1})=\mathrm{argmax}(b_{i}^{s}), contradicting the choice of ss. Therefore step ss must have been accepted as a triggered update with a nonempty witness set W≠∅W\neq\emptyset satisfying W⊆𝒯⁡(Eis)W\subseteq\mathcal{T}(E_{i}^{s}) and witnessing some trigger φi,j\varphi_{i,j}. ∎

Remark 11.

Theorem 17 gives trace-level licensing under faithful numerical enforcement. Witness tokens identify the evidence policy under which the step was accepted. They do not establish that token content alone caused the change, that the content was true, or that an auditor can infer the unknown ground truth. Section 9.7 gives an assumption-relative classification of correctness loss.

Figure 6 summarizes the router normal-form theorem: under the extractor and faithful-execution hypotheses of Theorem 8, the nonempty gate yields the explicitly evidence-gated behavior.

Sufficient logs for replay.

Token invariance permits omission of rhetorical text only when the remaining record contains every transition dependency. Record full annotated token exposures, all rounds including rejection/fallback, initial state, contracts and validator versions, public context/time, and any random routing outcomes. A witness subset is insufficient unless the operator and routing decision factor through it. For example, a trigger witnessed by W={a}W=\{a\} can use a token-invariant operator that sets b⁡(h)=0.6b(h)=0.6 on exposure {a}\{a\} and b⁡(h)=0.9b(h)=0.9 on exposure {a,b}\{a,b\}.

Proposition 6 (Replay from sufficient inputs).

Suppose bit+1=Fi​(bit,Xit,cit,rit)b_{i}^{t+1}=F_{i}(b_{i}^{t},X_{i}^{t},c_{i}^{t},r_{i}^{t}) is deterministic, where XitX_{i}^{t} is full annotated exposure, citc_{i}^{t} is public context, and ritr_{i}^{t} records routing or validation choices not determined by the other inputs. The initial state and these inputs for every round determine the trajectory. Witness-only replay is valid only under an additional factorization of this transition through the logged witness/payload and context.

Proof.

The supplied inputs determine the first successor; induction determines every subsequent state. Under the additional factorization, substitute the witness-based transition at each step. ∎

Remark 12 (Enforcement as semantic projection).

The router normal-form results (Theorems 8 and 9) make the “output gate” semantics precise: once enforcement rejects unauditable (empty-witness) steps, any auditable trigger protocol behaves as if all of its non-fallback behavior were explicitly evidence-gated. In this sense, external enforcement projects arbitrary deliberation protocols down to the evidential PBRC shape.

Remark 13 (Why audit equivalence matters).

Belief equivalence alone says two protocols behave the same internally. Audit equivalence strengthens this: an external compliance gate that only accepts nonempty-witness certificates will accept/reject the same updates under PiP_{i} and under NF⁡(Pi)\mathrm{NF}(P_{i}). Thus NF⁡(Pi)\mathrm{NF}(P_{i}) is a canonical “PBRC-shaped” realization of the same auditable behavior.

Remark 14 (Interaction with minimality theorems).

If PiP_{i} additionally satisfies evidence-free peer-pressure immunity and evidence-free non-amplification, then the social-only behavior absorbed into δiNF\delta_{i}^{\mathrm{NF}} must be argmax-preserving and non-amplifying on social-only events. Combined with Theorems 4–6, the compiled fallback retains these behavioral properties. This supports the chosen representation, but does not imply that robust protocols must originally have evidence-gated trigger syntax.

9 Adversary models and conditional robustness bounds

Evidence gating controls admissibility, not the truth or representativeness of evidence. The results below separate assumptions about evidence availability, authentication, semantic accuracy, context, and numerical execution. Language is inert under the token-invariance assumptions of Theorem 10; sound routing alone does not make every evidence-bearing contract insensitive to language.

9.1 Threat taxonomy

Definition 34 (Token appearance history).

Seen<t​(τ)\mathrm{Seen}_{<t}(\tau) holds when some message transmitted strictly before round tt contained τ\tau. Initial possession is recorded separately.

Definition 35 (No-new-valid-evidence adversary).

An adversary has no new valid evidence if every valid token it transmits has either been recorded initially or appeared earlier in the run. This is an availability restriction, stronger than ordinary signature unforgeability: an adversary may obtain and transmit a genuinely signed output for the first time without forging anything.

Definition 36 (Evidence-interface forgery).

A forgery is an adversarial artifact accepted as authentic by the validity layer although it lacks the required authentic origin or authorization. An authentic but false tool result is a semantic integrity failure, not necessarily a signature forgery.

Definition 37 (Replay adversary).

A replay adversary retransmits issued tokens without modifying their authenticated contents, potentially outside their intended time, instance, or use count.

Definition 38 (Colluding adversary).

A colluding adversary coordinates controlled agents or validators, including their evidence selection and attestations.

Definition 39 (Omission/delay adversary).

An omission/delay adversary withholds, delays, or selectively forwards evidence. This can obstruct correction or cause biased evidence-bearing updates; it is not exclusively a liveness attack.

9.2 Evidence-generation steering and omission attacks

Tokens are exogenous inputs to the present operational model. In an application, social messages can influence retrieval queries and tool inputs and thereby change which authentic tokens are generated. Selectively retaining supporting results can also produce a misleading evidence stream. The token-empty invariants survive omission, but correctness under evidence-bearing events needs additional assumptions. Authentication alone establishes neither balanced acquisition nor semantic truth.

A possible extension binds tokens to tool inputs and instance identifiers and adds a QueryOK\mathrm{QueryOK} predicate for a preregistered acquisition policy. Mandatory counter-evidence queries require an auditable record of required queries, returned results, and omissions. This is a proposed extension; the present experiments do not implement or validate it.

9.3 No-evidence robustness

Theorem 18 (Immunity in an initially token-empty system).

Suppose the initial system contains no valid tokens, neither honest agents nor the environment generate new valid tokens, and adversaries satisfy Definition 35. If honest agents use evidential contracts, sound enforcement, faithful numerical execution, and argmax-preserving fallback, their top sets remain unchanged. If fallback is also confidence-nonincreasing, their maximal confidence cannot increase.

Proof.

Induction on rounds shows that no transmitted token is valid: none exists initially, none is generated honestly, and an adversary cannot introduce a first valid token. Every exposure is therefore social-only. Evidential triggers are false, sound enforcement selects fallback, and the two conclusions follow by induction using the fallback properties. ∎

9.4 Limits under evidence-interface compromise

Theorem 19 (Conditional effect of an accepted forged witness).

Fix a reachable belief bb and an adversarially deliverable event EE. Suppose branch jj is the full-event priority-selected branch, the adversary can supply a certificate passing every required check, the router accepts it, and numerical execution applies Uj​(b,E)U_{j}(b,E). If Uj​(b,E)U_{j}(b,E) has a specified adverse property (for example, a false unique maximizer), that property holds after the step even if the certificate’s accepted evidence was forged.

Proof.

Acceptance and faithful numerical execution give b′=Uj​(b,E)b^{\prime}=U_{j}(b,E). Substitute this equality into the assumed adverse property. ∎

This conditional boundary result does not imply that forgeability alone forces a false belief. Rejection, a higher-priority branch, incomplete routing, or an operator that preserves correctness may prevent the hypothesized transition. Cryptographic integrity and semantic accuracy must be assessed separately.

9.5 Replay and freshness

Definition 40 (Freshness and context).

For an authenticated issue time Time⁡(τ)\mathrm{Time}(\tau) and window Δ≥0\Delta\geq 0, define

FreshΔ​(τ,t)⇔0≤t−Time⁡(τ)≤Δ.\mathrm{Fresh}_{\Delta}(\tau,t)\iff 0\leq t-\mathrm{Time}(\tau)\leq\Delta.

A separate predicate ContextMatch⁡(τ,c)\mathrm{ContextMatch}(\tau,c) binds the token to the current task, schema, and instance cc. Future-dated tokens fail freshness.

Theorem 20 (Expiry of replayed evidence).

Suppose every accepted evidence token must be valid, fresh, and context-matching, and replay cannot change authenticated timestamps. A token issued at rr cannot be used at t<rt<r or t>r+Δt>r+\Delta. If all available tokens have issue times at most ss and no later tokens become available, replay alone cannot enable an evidential branch at any t>s+Δt>s+\Delta.

Proof.

The first assertion is exactly the freshness inequality. For the second, every available token has t−Time⁡(τ)>Δt-\mathrm{Time}(\tau)>\Delta, so no nonempty accepted evidence witness exists. ∎

Freshness does not prevent repeated use within the window. Avoiding repeated likelihood multiplication requires deduplication, an idempotent operator, or an authenticated spent-token ledger included in the state and replay record. Fixed-validity flooding results do not directly cover expiry or such additional state.

9.6 Multi-attestation under explicit integrity assumptions

Definition 41 (kk-of-KK validity).

Let Attest⁡(τ,s)\mathrm{Attest}(\tau,s) mean a verified attestation on the complete token and context from authenticated validator identity s∈{1,…,K}s\in\{1,\ldots,K\}. Define

Validk​(τ)⇔|{s:Attest⁡(τ,s)}|≥k,1≤k≤K.\mathrm{Valid}_{k}(\tau)\iff|\{s:\mathrm{Attest}(\tau,s)\}|\geq k,\qquad 1\leq k\leq K.

Repeated signatures from the same identity count once.

Theorem 21 (Independent-compromise bound).

Over a fixed attack horizon, suppose each validator is compromised independently with probability pp, uncompromised signatures cannot be forged, and uncompromised validators never attest to the target false assertion in its bound context. Then the probability that the adversary can obtain kk accepted distinct attestations for that false assertion is at most

∑j=kK(Kj)​pj​(1−p)K−j.\sum_{j=k}^{K}\binom{K}{j}p^{j}(1-p)^{K-j}.
Proof.

Success requires at least kk compromised identities. Their count has the Binomial⁡(K,p)\mathrm{Binomial}(K,p) distribution. The success event is a subset of its upper-tail event. ∎

Proposition 7 (Deterministic compromise threshold).

Under the same authentication and honest-validator truth assumptions, at most ff compromised validators cannot authorize the target false assertion when k>fk>f.

Proof.

Only compromised validators can supply an accepted attestation to that assertion, giving at most ff distinct identities. ∎

These bounds do not cover correlated semantic errors, shared sources, or honest validators deceived into signing false claims. A numerical attestation count supplied by an untrusted model is not authenticated multi-attestation.

9.7 A conditional failure taxonomy

Definition 42 (Correct belief state).

Fix h⋆∈ℋh^{\star}\in\mathcal{H}. Write Correct⁡(b)\mathrm{Correct}(b) iff h⋆∈argmax⁡(b)h^{\star}\in\mathrm{argmax}(b). This allows ties and does not guarantee that a separate tie-breaking answer rule returns h⋆h^{\star}.

Definition 43 (Applicability and token soundness).

At time tt and context ctc_{t}, let

App⁡(τ,t)=Valid⁡(τ)∧FreshΔ​(τ,t)∧ContextMatch⁡(τ,ct).\mathrm{App}(\tau,t)=\mathrm{Valid}(\tau)\land\mathrm{Fresh}_{\Delta}(\tau,t)\land\mathrm{ContextMatch}(\tau,c_{t}).

Let TokSoundh⋆​(τ)\mathrm{TokSound}_{h^{\star}}(\tau) mean that τ\tau neither contradicts h⋆h^{\star} nor supports a false hypothesis. This is a truth-relative specification, not a computable consequence of signature validity.

Definition 44 (Evidence integrity and contract soundness).

Evidence integrity means that every applicable token is truth-sound. A contract is (h⋆,Δ)(h^{\star},\Delta)-sound if, for every correct input belief, full event, and accepted witness for the priority-selected branch, applicability and truth-soundness of all witness tokens imply correctness of the specified output operator. This condition quantifies over the whole event whenever the operator uses it. Fallback is separately required to preserve correctness.

Theorem 22 (First-error classification).

Assume an initially correct state, an evidential contract, argmax-preserving fallback, and a gate rejecting empty accepted witnesses. At a first transition from a correct state to an incorrect one, at least one of the following holds:

  1. 1.

    numerical execution differs from the specified accepted operator or fallback;

  2. 2.

    an accepted certificate fails full-event truth, priority, witness correctness, or valid-token membership;

  3. 3.

    an accepted witness token fails freshness or context matching;

  4. 4.

    an applicable accepted witness token is not truth-sound;

  5. 5.

    the selected operator fails contract soundness on the actual event and input state.

If numerical execution is faithful, the first incorrect transition is non-fallback and carries a nonempty accepted witness.

Proof.

If execution is unfaithful, case 1 holds. Otherwise an argmax-preserving fallback cannot remove h⋆h^{\star} from the top set. The step therefore accepted a branch with a nonempty witness. If any certificate check fails, case 2 holds. Otherwise its tokens are valid. If a token is stale or context-mismatched, case 3 holds; if all are applicable but one is not truth-sound, case 4 holds. In the remaining case all witness tokens are applicable and truth-sound, yet the selected specified operator maps a correct belief to an incorrect belief. This is precisely case 5. ∎

This is an exhaustive conditional classification, not an algorithm that identifies a unique cause from a certificate. The cases can overlap; evaluating truth-soundness requires external ground truth, and omitted evidence may be causally relevant.

Corollary 7 (Conditional preservation of correctness).

If execution is faithful, routing is sound, all accepted witnesses are applicable, evidence integrity holds, the contract is (h⋆,Δ)(h^{\star},\Delta)-sound, and fallback preserves argmax, an initially correct run remains correct.

Proof.

Each possible first-error case in Theorem 22 is excluded. ∎

Corollary 8 (First-error trace under equal exposures).

Under all assumptions of Theorem 16, two topologies with equal incoming token exposure traces and the same initial beliefs have identical beliefs and canonical accepted certificates. Consequently the first loss of correctness, if any, has the same index and canonical certificate in both. If the applicability annotations also agree, the classification above agrees as a truth-relative statement.

Proof.

Apply the equality of belief and canonical certificate traces from Theorem 16, then evaluate the same correctness predicate and classification on their identical inputs. Equal positive-walk reachability sets suffice for equal exposures by Theorem 13. ∎

10 Contractual Dynamic Doxastic Logic (CDDL) with iteration

10.1 Positioning and semantic interface

CDDL combines KD45 belief modalities with PDL programs and iteration as a specification language; the modal ingredients are standard [Harel et al.(2000), van Benthem and Smets(2015), Leitgeb and Segerberg(2007), Schmidt and Tishkovsky(2008)]. Our contribution here is the explicit interface to PBRC decisions and audit states. We prove soundness and exact checking on supplied finite models. We do not claim a new all-model completeness theorem or finite model property for the combined system.

10.2 Instrumented executions and abstraction atoms

Definition 45 (Abstraction map and action labeling).

For a recorded run with TT transitions, let states be indices 0,…,T0,\ldots,T. At each t<Tt<T record the full event EitE_{i}^{t}, input belief bitb_{i}^{t}, router decision, certificate, and output bit+1b_{i}^{t+1}. Set

𝖳𝗋𝗂𝗀i,j​(t)\displaystyle\mathsf{Trig}_{i,j}(t) ⇔𝒮⁡(Eit)⊧φi,j,\displaystyle\iff\mathcal{S}(E_{i}^{t})\models\varphi_{i,j}, 𝖲𝗈𝖼𝖮𝗇𝗅𝗒i​(t)\displaystyle\mathsf{SocOnly}_{i}(t) ⇔SocialOnly⁡(Eit),\displaystyle\iff\mathrm{SocialOnly}(E_{i}^{t}),
𝖳𝗈𝗉i,h​(t)\displaystyle\mathsf{Top}_{i,h}(t) ⇔h∈argmax⁡(bit),\displaystyle\iff h\in\mathrm{argmax}(b_{i}^{t}), 𝖠𝖼𝖼i,j​(t)\displaystyle\mathsf{Acc}_{i,j}(t) ⇔the router accepts branch ​j.\displaystyle\iff\text{the router accepts branch }j.

Define 𝖠𝖼𝖼i=⋁j𝖠𝖼𝖼i,j\mathsf{Acc}_{i}=\bigvee_{j}\mathsf{Acc}_{i,j}. Acceptance atoms label the source state of the decision. Put (t,t+1)(t,t+1) in R𝗎𝗉𝖽i,jR_{\mathsf{upd}_{i,j}} exactly when branch jj is accepted, and in R𝖿𝖻iR_{\mathsf{fb}_{i}} exactly when fallback executes. For each agent and recorded step exactly one such edge is required. At TT, top atoms use biTb_{i}^{T}; no outgoing step exists and the unused event/acceptance atoms can be set false.

This abstraction records behavior even if a contract violation is found; validation of that behavior is a separate audit check. The numerical probability vector does not determine a KD45 accessibility relation. Checking formulas containing BiB_{i} requires an explicitly supplied epistemic model. Practical run-log monitoring below uses the fragment without BiB_{i}.

10.3 Syntax

Fix agents 𝒜\mathcal{A}, propositional atoms 𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉\mathsf{Prop}, and atomic actions 𝖠𝖼𝗍0\mathsf{Act}_{0}.

Formulas.
φ::=p​∣¬φ​∣(φ∧φ)∣​Bi​φ∣​[α]​φ,\varphi::=p\mid\neg\varphi\mid(\varphi\land\varphi)\mid B_{i}\varphi\mid[\alpha]\varphi,
